title: Fennel gratin
intro: Tender fennel under béchamel and a golden Parmesan crust.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Remove the tough outer layers of the fennel and cut each bulb into 8 wedges.

airfryer.t: Remove the tough outer layers of the fennel and cut each bulb into 8 wedges.

steps.t: Boil the wedges in salted water for 8 minutes, until tender but still firm.
steps.label: Fennel

steps.t: Drain well and pat dry on a towel, or the gratin will be watery.
Butter a baking dish, lay the fennel in a single layer and season with salt and pepper.
Cover with the béchamel (store-bought is fine), then the Parmesan, breadcrumbs and dots of butter.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp on top.
steps.label: Bake

airfryer.t: Set the dish in the basket and air-fry at 180 °C for 15 minutes, until golden.

steps.t: Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Lighter version: skip the béchamel and use just melted butter, Parmesan and breadcrumbs.
Add a little orange zest or a few fennel seeds to the béchamel.

title: Sautéed chicory
intro: Southern Italian chicory, blanched then sautéed with garlic, oil and chili.

steps.t: Trim off the tough bases of the chicory and wash it in several changes of water until no grit remains.
Boil in plenty of salted water for 10 minutes, until the stems are tender.
steps.label: Chicory

steps.t: Drain, let it cool a little, squeeze out the water by hand and chop roughly.
Warm the oil in a pan with the crushed garlic and chili for 2 minutes, until the garlic is golden.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Add the chicory and sauté for 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring; season with salt.
steps.label: Sauté

tips.t: The more water you boil it in, the less bitter it stays; drain as soon as the stems are tender.
Serve on a dried fava bean purée for the Puglian classic "fave e cicorie".
Melt an anchovy fillet in the oil with the garlic.

title: Zucchini scapece
intro: Neapolitan fried zucchini, marinated with vinegar, garlic and mint.

steps.t: Slice the zucchini into 3 mm rounds and spread them on a towel to dry for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Dry

steps.t: Heat the oil to 170 °C and fry the zucchini in batches for 4 minutes, until golden in patches.
steps.label: Fry

airfryer.t: Toss the zucchini with 1 tbsp oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 15 minutes, shaking halfway.

steps.t: Drain on paper towels and salt them.
Layer them in a shallow dish with sliced garlic, mint leaves and a sprinkle of vinegar.
Let them marinate for at least 1 hour at room temperature before serving.
steps.label: Marinate

tips.t: Even better the next day; covered in the fridge they keep 3 days.
Same method works with sliced eggplant, just as classic in Naples.

title: Ratatouille
intro: Provence's summer vegetable stew, each vegetable cooked alone, then together.

steps.t: Cut all the vegetables into 2 cm cubes; peel and chop the tomatoes.
Brown the eggplant in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, until golden, then set aside.
steps.label: Eggplant

steps.t: Sauté the zucchini in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes and set aside.
steps.label: Zucchini

steps.t: In a wide pot, soften the onion and peppers in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Peppers

steps.t: Add the garlic, tomatoes, thyme and bay leaf and cook for 10 minutes, until saucy.
steps.label: Tomatoes

steps.t: Return the eggplant and zucchini, cover and simmer on low for 25 minutes, stirring gently.
steps.label: Simmer

oven.t: Transfer everything to a baking dish with the eggplant and zucchini and bake at 180 °C for 45 minutes.

steps.t: Remove the herbs, season with salt, drizzle with the remaining oil and finish with basil.

tips.t: Cooking each vegetable separately is the secret: each keeps its shape and flavor.
Better the next day; reheat and top with a poached egg.
Use 1 tsp herbes de Provence instead of thyme for a deeper aroma.

title: Aloo gobi
intro: Punjabi spiced cauliflower and potatoes with turmeric and cumin.

steps.t: Break the cauliflower into florets and cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and let the cumin seeds sizzle for 30 seconds.
steps.label: Cumin

steps.t: Add the chopped onion and cook for 6 minutes, until golden.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the grated ginger and garlic, chili, turmeric and coriander, then the chopped tomatoes; cook 4 minutes.
steps.label: Masala

steps.t: Add the potatoes, cauliflower, salt and water, stir, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, until tender.
steps.label: Cook

oven.t: Toss the potatoes and cauliflower with the masala and salt, spread on a tray and roast at 210 °C for 30 minutes.

steps.t: Uncover, turn up the heat and cook 3 minutes, until dry and lightly browned.
steps.label: Dry

oven.t: Take out when the vegetables are tender and browned at the edges.

steps.t: Stir in the garam masala and chopped cilantro and serve.

tips.t: Serve with basmati rice and lentil dal, or with warm naan.
Stir gently and not too often so the florets stay whole.

title: German red cabbage
intro: Festive Rotkohl: red cabbage braised sweet and sour with apples.

steps.t: Quarter the cabbage, cut out the core and slice thinly; peel and dice the apples and slice the onion.
Heat the oil in a large pot and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the sugar and let it caramelize for 2 minutes, stirring.
steps.label: Caramel

steps.t: Add the cabbage, apples and vinegar and stir for 3 minutes, until the cabbage starts to wilt.
steps.label: Cabbage

steps.t: Pour in the apple juice, add the bay leaves, cloves and salt, cover and braise on low for 1 hour.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Add the juice, spices and salt, seal the pressure cooker and cook for 15 minutes at high pressure.

steps.t: Remove the spices and balance the sweet-sour taste with salt, sugar or vinegar.

tips.t: Freezes perfectly, and reheated the next day it tastes even better.
Serve with roast pork, duck or bread dumplings, the German Christmas plate.
Stir in a spoonful of redcurrant jelly at the end for gloss and depth.

title: Farofa, toasted cassava flour
intro: Cassava flour toasted in butter with onion, the crunchy topping for everything.

steps.t: Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium-low heat and cook the chopped onion until golden.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the chopped garlic and cook for 30 seconds without letting it brown.
Sprinkle in the cassava flour and toast it, stirring constantly, until golden, sandy and nutty-smelling.
steps.label: Toast

steps.t: Season with salt, stir in the chopped parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips.t: Farofa de bacon: crisp 100 g diced smoked bacon before adding the onion.
Medium heat and keep stirring: cassava flour goes from golden to burnt in seconds.
Sprinkle it over feijoada or serve next to picanha.

title: Couve à mineira, sautéed kale
intro: Kale cut into fine ribbons and flash-fried with garlic, Minas Gerais style.

steps.t: Wash the kale, strip out the central rib and dry the leaves well.
Stack the leaves, roll them tightly like a cigar and slice into very thin 2 mm ribbons.
Warm the oil with the chopped garlic in a wide pan until fragrant, without letting it color.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Add the kale and salt and toss over high heat until bright green and just wilted but still crisp.
steps.label: Kale

steps.t: Serve straight away, before it loses its color.

tips.t: The thinner the ribbons, the less cooking: 3 minutes keeps it green and crisp.
In Minas they often crisp a little diced smoked bacon first.
It's the must-have side for feijoada: the greens lighten the beans.

title: Rau muống xào tỏi, garlic greens
intro: Leafy greens tossed over high heat with lots of garlic, ready in 5 minutes.

steps.t: Wash the greens and drain well. Cut the pak choi into 5 cm pieces, keeping stems and leaves apart.
Crush the garlic and chop it roughly.
Heat the oil in a wok over the highest heat and fry half the garlic for 20 seconds, until fragrant and just golden.
Add the stems with the salt and sugar and toss for 2 minutes.
steps.label: Stems

steps.t: Add the leaves and water and toss for 1 minute, just until wilted but still bright green.
steps.label: Leaves

steps.t: Turn off the heat, stir in the rest of the garlic raw and serve at once with the pan juices.

tips.t: With real rau muống (water spinach) from Asian shops, the hollow stems stay crunchy.
Many cooks add a teaspoon of fish sauce at the end: more savoury, but no longer vegan.

title: Phat phak ruam, mixed vegetable stir-fry
intro: Mixed vegetables tossed over fierce heat with garlic and soy, glossy and crisp.

steps.t: Cut the vegetables into bite-sized pieces: carrots in diagonal slices, pepper in strips, mushrooms halved, corn and pak choi in chunks.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar and 4 tbsp water in a cup. Crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in the wok over the highest heat and fry the garlic for 15 seconds, until golden.
Add the carrots and broccoli with 2 tbsp water and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
steps.label: Broccoli

steps.t: Add the pepper, mushrooms and baby corn and stir-fry 2 more minutes.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add the pak choi and sauce and toss for 1 minute, until the leaves wilt and everything is glossy but crisp.
steps.label: Pak choi

steps.t: Serve straight away, with jasmine rice.

tips.t: Maximum heat and a wok that isn't crowded: the veg should sear, not stew. For 4, cook in two batches.
Restaurants use oyster sauce; Thai vegan (jay) cooking uses the mushroom sauce sold in Asian shops.

title: Loubieh bi zeit, beans in olive oil
intro: Green beans slowly braised in olive oil and tomato, eaten at room temperature.

steps.t: Trim the beans and cut them into 4-5 cm pieces; chop the onion and slice the garlic.
Heat the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion over medium heat until soft and golden, adding the garlic for the last minute.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the beans and stir until bright green and glossy with oil.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Add the chopped tomatoes, allspice, salt, pepper and water. Cover and cook over low heat until the beans are very tender.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Add tomatoes, allspice, salt, pepper and water, close the pressure cooker and cook 8 minutes once at pressure.

steps.t: Uncover and reduce the sauce for 5 minutes if it's still watery.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: Let it cool slightly and serve at room temperature, with pita.

tips.t: In Lebanon flat runner beans are used: if you find them, they're even tastier.
Don't skimp on the oil: together with the tomato, it makes the sauce.
Like all bi zeit dishes it's better the next day and keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Di san xian, aubergine, potato, pepper
intro: Fried aubergine, potato and green pepper tossed in garlic sauce, a northeastern classic.

steps.t: Cut the aubergines into irregular chunks, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and leave to stand.
steps.label: Aubergine

steps.t: Meanwhile peel the potatoes and cut into thin wedges; cut the pepper into pieces, chop the garlic and spring onion.
Mix the soy, sugar, water and 1 tsp cornflour. Pat the aubergine dry and dust with the remaining cornflour.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and fry the potatoes until golden and tender. Drain on paper.
steps.label: Potatoes

airfryer.t: Toss the potatoes in 1 tbsp oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 18 minutes, shaking halfway.

steps.t: Fry the aubergine until golden and soft, adding the pepper for the last 20 seconds. Drain.
steps.label: Aubergine

airfryer.t: Toss the aubergine and pepper in a little oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 15 minutes, shaking halfway.

steps.t: Pour off all but 1 tbsp oil, fry the garlic and spring onion, then add the veg and sauce and toss until everything is glossy.

tips.t: The cornflour coating gives the aubergine a thin crust: it soaks up less oil and holds the sauce.
Swap the soy sauce for tamari and it's gluten-free too.

title: Sigeumchi namul, sesame spinach
intro: Blanched spinach dressed with garlic and sesame: the simplest, best-loved banchan.

steps.t: Bring plenty of water to the boil with half the salt and blanch the washed spinach until just wilted.
steps.label: Spinach

steps.t: Drain, plunge into cold water and squeeze out firmly by the handful to remove all the water.
Cut into 5 cm lengths; finely mince the garlic and spring onion and lightly crush the sesame seeds.
Toss with your hands with the garlic, spring onion, sesame oil, sesame seeds and remaining salt. Serve at room temperature.

tips.t: Squeeze the spinach hard: if it stays wet, the dressing gets watered down.
It keeps for 2 days in the fridge in a sealed container, like all banchan.

title: Ingen no gomaae, sesame green beans
intro: Crisp green beans in a sweet and savoury dressing of toasted, crushed sesame.

steps.t: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and trim the beans.
Blanch them for 3 minutes, until bright green and still crisp.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Drain into iced water, then dry them well and cut into 4 cm lengths.
Toast the sesame in a dry pan over medium heat, shaking, until golden and starting to pop.
steps.label: Sesame

steps.t: Grind it in a mortar while still warm until half-crushed and fragrant, then stir in the sugar and soy sauce.
Toss the beans with the sesame dressing just before serving, at room temperature.

tips.t: Dress them at the last minute: soy draws out water and the sesame loses its crunch.
Made with blanched, squeezed spinach it becomes hōrensō no gomaae, another classic.
No mortar? Pulse in a spice grinder: it should stay gritty, not turn to paste.

title: Frijoles de olla (pot beans)
intro: Black beans simmered slowly with onion and garlic, creamy and served in their broth.

steps.t: Rinse the beans, picking out any stones, and soak them in plenty of cold water (overnight is fine).
steps.label: Soaking

steps.t: Drain and put them in a pot with the water, half the onion, the whole garlic and bay leaf, no salt; bring to a boil.

pressure.t: Drain and put them in the pressure cooker with 1.5 l water, half the onion, garlic and bay leaf, no salt.

steps.t: Simmer half-covered over low heat until creamy, adding hot water if they peek out.
steps.label: Beans

pressure.t: Lock the lid and cook 30 minutes at pressure over low heat, then let it release naturally.

steps.t: Add the salt and cook uncovered so the broth thickens slightly.
steps.label: Broth

steps.t: Remove the onion and bay leaf and serve in small bowls with broth, the rest of the onion chopped and cilantro.

tips.t: In Mexico a sprig of epazote goes in at the end: look for it dried in Latin shops.
The next day mash them in a pan with a little oil to make frijoles refritos.

title: Briam (Greek roasted vegetables)
intro: Potatoes, zucchini, eggplant and peppers slow-baked with tomato and olive oil.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the potatoes, zucchini and eggplant into chunks, the pepper into strips and onions into wedges.
Grate 2 tomatoes and mix the pulp with chopped garlic, oil, oregano, parsley, salt and pepper.
In a large dish toss the vegetables with the raw sauce, top with the other tomatoes, sliced, and add the water.
Cover with foil and bake.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Uncover, gently turn the vegetables and bake until golden and the juices have reduced.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Let it rest: briam is best warm, with bread to soak up the oil.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Cut the potatoes smaller than the other vegetables so everything cooks at the same time.
If it need not be vegan, a slab of feta alongside makes it a full meal.
It tastes even better the next day at room temperature.

title: Pisto manchego, Spanish vegetable stew
intro: Peppers, zucchini and onion cooked slowly in tomato until almost jammy.

steps.t: Cut the onions, peppers and zucchini into 1 cm dice; grate the tomatoes and discard the skins.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onions and chopped garlic over low heat until soft and translucent.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the peppers and cook over medium-low heat until tender.
steps.label: Peppers

steps.t: Add the zucchini and a pinch of salt and keep cooking, stirring now and then.
steps.label: Zucchini

steps.t: Pour in the tomato and sugar and cook uncovered over low heat, stirring, until thick with no liquid left.
steps.label: Tomato

steps.t: Taste, adjust the salt and serve hot or warm.

tips.t: Add the vegetables one at a time, in this order: each keeps its flavour and nothing turns to mush.
Top with a fried egg and serve with bread for a classic supper from La Mancha.
It's even better the next day; warm on a slice of bread it becomes a tapa.

title: Vichy carrots
intro: Carrot coins cooked in a little water with butter and sugar until glossy and sweet.

ing.n: water (mineral water if you have it)

steps.t: Peel the carrots and slice them into 3 mm coins, all the same so they cook evenly.
Put them in a wide pan with the butter, sugar, salt and water: they should be just covered.
Cover with a circle of baking paper and cook over medium heat until tender and the water has nearly gone.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Remove the paper and toss over high heat until the liquid turns into a shiny glaze that coats them.
steps.label: Glaze

steps.t: Sprinkle with parsley, taste for salt and serve at once.

tips.t: In France they use bicarbonate-rich Vichy water: a pinch of baking soda in the water makes them just as tender.
They go well with roasts, chicken and especially bœuf bourguignon.
Instead of parsley, try a little chopped chervil or tarragon.
